narration: If you've got multiple debts, the order you pay them off matters more than how fast. And most people get this completely backwards.
visual: Three credit cards spring in one by one on dark background. Each shows balance and APR: $2,000 at 18%, $6,000 at 22%, $3,000 at 27%. The 27% card pulses red.

narration: The most popular strategy is the debt snowball — you wipe out the smallest balance first. It feels incredible when that card hits zero, but your wallet absolutely hates it.
visual: A snowball grows and rolls across a light background, knocking out the small $2,000 card with a green checkmark. Dollar signs float upward and vanish — wasted interest on higher-rate debts still compounding.

narration: The debt avalanche targets your highest interest rate first — not the smallest balance. A magnifying glass locks onto that 27% card. That's the one bleeding you dry.
visual: Three debt cards on dark background ranked last, second, first by attack order. A magnifying glass slides to focus on the 27% card. It pulses and reads ATTACK FIRST.

narration: Same three debts, different order. The snowball racks up over twenty-two thousand in total interest. The avalanche cuts it to eight thousand. That's fourteen grand back in your pocket.
visual: Split comparison on light background: left column SNOWBALL showing $22,400 total interest in red, right column AVALANCHE showing $8,400 in green. An animated counter below counts up to $14,000 difference.

narration: Here's why nobody switches — your brain craves quick wins. Knocking out a small debt floods you with dopamine. Banks spend billions making sure you chase that feeling instead of the math.
visual: Purple brain SVG glowing with dopamine sparkles on dark background. Dollar signs flow rightward into a bank building. Text overlay: BANKS PROFIT FROM THIS BIAS.

narration: Tonight: list every debt, sort by interest rate highest to lowest, and throw every extra dollar at number one. That one reorder is worth fourteen thousand dollars — try it right now.
visual: Three debts slide onto a light background sorted 1-2-3 by rate: 27%, 22%, 18%. First item glows red with an ATTACK NOW badge. Final callout box: SAVE $14,000 — just by changing the order.
